templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Please do not lean out of the window while the train is moving.'
Assumption I: People may lean out of the window.
Assumption II: It is dangerous to lean out of a moving train.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The notice assumes people may lean out (I) — otherwise the notice is unnecessary. It also assumes leaning is dangerous (II) — that's the reason for the notice. Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Eat an apple a day to stay healthy.'
Assumption I: Apples are available in the market.
Assumption II: People want to stay healthy.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The advice assumes people want to stay healthy (II) — the motivation to follow it. Assumption I (availability) is too general and not necessary for the advice. Only II is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The government has decided to ban all single-use plastics.'
Assumption I: Single-use plastics cause environmental harm.
Assumption II: Citizens will comply with the ban.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The ban assumes plastic causes harm (I) — reason for the action. It also assumes citizens will comply (II) — otherwise the ban is pointless. Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Join our coaching centre for guaranteed success in competitive exams.'
Assumption I: Students want to succeed in competitive exams.
Assumption II: No other coaching centre provides such guarantee.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Students wanting success (I) is implicit — it's the target audience's desire. Assumption II is not implicit — it is a competitive claim, not assumed in the statement. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Drink boiled water to avoid water-borne diseases.'
Assumption I: Boiling kills harmful germs in water.
Assumption II: People are currently suffering from water-borne diseases.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Boiling kills germs (I) is the basis of the advice — implicit. Assumption II (currently suffering) is too specific and not assumed. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Use helmet while riding a two-wheeler.'
Assumption I: Riding without helmet is dangerous.
Assumption II: People ride two-wheelers.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Both are implicit. The instruction assumes people ride two-wheelers (II) — target audience. It also assumes it is dangerous without helmet (I) — reason for the advice.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The best way to learn a language is to speak it every day.'
Assumption I: Speaking daily improves language skills.
Assumption II: People want to learn a new language.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The statement is advice for people learning a language, so it assumes people want to learn (II). It also assumes speaking daily is effective (I). Both implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Children should be given nutritious food for proper growth.'
Assumption I: Nutritious food supports physical and mental growth.
Assumption II: Children currently do not get nutritious food.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The link between nutrition and growth (I) is the foundation of the statement — implicit. Assumption II assumes a current deficiency which is too specific. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'If you want a bright career, study hard from early age.'
Assumption I: Early study leads to a better career.
Assumption II: Everyone wants a bright career.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The statement uses 'if you want' — so it doesn't assume everyone wants it (II not implicit). The causal link between early study and career (I) is assumed. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Books are the best companions of man.'
Assumption I: Man needs companions.
Assumption II: Books provide knowledge and entertainment.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Calling books companions assumes man needs companions (I) and that books serve that role (II). Both are implicit in the statement.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Do not park your vehicle in front of the hospital entrance.'
Assumption I: Vehicles are parked in front of hospitals.
Assumption II: Parking in front of hospitals causes obstruction.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The notice implies people may park there (I) — otherwise the notice is irrelevant. It assumes parking causes obstruction (II) — the reason for the notice. Both implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Aerobics is the best exercise to reduce weight.'
Assumption I: Exercise can reduce weight.
Assumption II: People want to reduce weight.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Exercise reducing weight (I) is the basis of the statement. Saying 'best' to reduce weight assumes people want to reduce it (II). Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The municipal corporation has asked all residents to conserve water.'
Assumption I: There is a shortage of water in the city.
Assumption II: Residents can conserve water if they want to.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Asking people to conserve assumes they have the ability to do so (II) — implicit. A shortage (I) is a likely reason but not necessarily assumed — the request could be for future planning. Only II is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Switch off the lights when not in use to save electricity.'
Assumption I: Electricity is produced at some cost.
Assumption II: People sometimes leave lights on unnecessarily.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The advice implies people leave lights on unnecessarily (II) — target behaviour. That electricity needs to be saved (I) is also implicit. Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'To maintain good health, avoid junk food.'
Assumption I: Junk food is harmful to health.
Assumption II: People eat junk food regularly.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Junk food being harmful (I) is the foundation of the advice — implicit. Assumption II (people regularly eat junk food) is not assumed — the advice is general. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Kindly carry your identity card at all times during the examination.'
Assumption I: Students may forget to carry their identity cards.
Assumption II: Identity cards help verify the student's identity.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The reminder assumes students may forget (I) — reason for the reminder. Identity cards verifying identity (II) is the purpose — also implicit. Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Trees should be planted along roadsides.'
Assumption I: Trees provide shade and improve air quality.
Assumption II: Roadsides currently have no trees.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Trees providing benefits (I) is the reason for planting — implicit. Assumption II (no current trees) is not assumed — planting can happen even if some trees exist. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'An advertisement: Visit our new store for the best deals in town.'
Assumption I: People are looking for good deals.
Assumption II: The store has better deals than other stores.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: People looking for deals (I) is implicit — target audience motivation. The store having the best deals (II) is the claim being made, not an assumption. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Smoking is injurious to health — statutory warning on cigarette packs.'
Assumption I: People smoke cigarettes.
Assumption II: Warning messages discourage smoking.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: A warning on cigarette packs assumes people smoke (I). It also assumes warnings are effective (II) — otherwise, why put them? Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The school has arranged extra classes for students who failed the test.'
Assumption I: Extra classes will help improve students' performance.
Assumption II: The students who failed want to improve.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Extra classes helping (I) is the rationale — implicit. Assumption II (students want to improve) cannot be assumed from the school's arrangement. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'All passengers must fasten their seat belts during takeoff and landing.'
Assumption I: Seat belts improve passenger safety.
Assumption II: Some passengers may not fasten seat belts on their own.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Seat belts improving safety (I) is the reason for the rule — implicit. The rule implies some passengers may not comply on their own (II) — also implicit. Both are implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Start your day with a glass of warm lemon water for better digestion.'
Assumption I: Warm lemon water aids digestion.
Assumption II: Everyone has digestive problems.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Lemon water aiding digestion (I) is the basis of the advice — implicit. Assumption II (everyone has digestive problems) is too strong — the advice can be for general wellness. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'The government has launched a scheme to provide free mid-day meals in schools.'
Assumption I: Many school children are malnourished.
Assumption II: Free meals will attract more children to attend school.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Both are implicit. The scheme assumes some children are malnourished (I) — motivation for free meals. It also assumes meals improve attendance (II) — an expected outcome that justifies the scheme.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Read the instructions carefully before operating the machine.'
Assumption I: Operating without instructions may cause damage or injury.
Assumption II: The machine is difficult to operate.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: The instruction assumes risk without reading instructions (I) — the reason for the warning. That the machine is difficult (II) is not necessarily assumed — even simple machines need instructions. Only I is implicit.

templates.pattern:
Statement: 'Citizens should vote in every election to strengthen democracy.'
Assumption I: Voting strengthens democracy.
Assumption II: Many citizens do not vote.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
templates.explanation: Voting strengthening democracy (I) is the stated reason — implicit. Assumption II (many don't vote) explains why the appeal is made — also implicit. Both are implicit.
